blocks.text: Managing email volume in Outlook for Mac

Tax season creates a surge in email traffic. Clients send documents, ask for status updates, and request meetings. Managing this flow requires a structured approach. Use folders to categorize emails by client or tax status. You can create a new folder by selecting File > New Folder in the menu bar. This keeps your inbox clean and ensures you do not miss critical filings.

Keyboard shortcuts are essential for speed. Use ⌘ + 1 to switch to Mail, ⌘ + 2 for Calendar, and ⌘ + 3 for Contacts. If you need to draft a new message, press ⌘ + N. To send an email, press ⌘ + Return. These small actions add up when you process dozens of emails per hour.

Lazur lives in your Mac menu bar. It does not click buttons for you, but it acts as a guide. When you are lost in a complex menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for help. Lazur points to the menu item you need. This saves you from hunting for settings in the new Outlook interface.

Drafting the same responses to common client questions is repetitive. Use the dictation feature to speed up your writing. Hold the fn key to start dictating. Speak clearly and let Lazur format the text for you. This is useful for status updates or requesting missing forms. You can keep snippets of your most common replies to save even more time.

Meetings often interrupt your deep work time. Use the Calendar view to block off time for tax preparation. When a client requests a meeting, quickly create an invite by pressing ⌘ + N while in the Calendar view. If you find yourself spending too much time on post-meeting notes, ask Lazur to summarize your thoughts after you dictate them.

faq.question: Can Lazur fill out tax forms for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or interact with your tax software. It helps you navigate your Mac and draft emails.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with the new Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on your Mac, including the new Outlook interface.

faq.question: Is my client data safe with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur does not store your screen content or audio. Information is sent to AI providers only while you hold the shortcut key.
